stem:
Charu digs up a bean plant and an onion plant from the school garden. The bean plant has one thick main root with thinner side roots. The onion plant has many thin roots of nearly the same size and no single main root.

Which labelling is correct?

options.text: Bean has a taproot system; onion has a fibrous root system.
Bean has a fibrous root system; onion has a taproot system.
Both plants have taproot systems because both have roots in soil.
Both plants have fibrous root systems because both were dug from the garden.

teacher.key_rationale: One main root with side roots is a taproot (bean); many similar thin roots with no main root are fibrous (onion). Swapping those labels reverses the relationship; merely having roots in soil does not decide the type.
